description: Official (statutory / authoritative) processing-time ranges per immigration corridor. Used by processingTimeEstimate() (P2-04a) as the fallback source when platform case data is below the 20-case statistical-significance threshold. Maps low_days -> p50 and high_days -> p90 for the official_only branch.

source.title: Registration scheme for EU/EEA nationals — UDI (Norwegian Directorate of Immigration)

entries.notes: EEA registration: a decision is typically issued same-day at the police station, but the legal registration window spans up to 90 days from arrival. Range covers same-day through the full legal window.
Upper bound is the published statutory processing target (45 days). Lower bound reflects commonly observed expedited consulate processing.

source.title: EU Blue Card — Make it in Germany (federal Skilled Immigration portal)

secondary_sources.title: Visa for the purpose of employment — Auswärtiges Amt

entries.notes: Germany does not publish a single statutory numeric deadline for Blue Card visa processing — it is consulate-dependent. Range is the commonly cited 4–12 week consulate window (28–84 days). Fast-track (3–4 weeks) applies when the employer opts into the accelerated skilled-worker procedure.

source.title: EU Blue Card — Make it in Germany (federal Skilled Immigration portal)

secondary_sources.title: Visa for the purpose of employment — Auswärtiges Amt

entries.notes: Post-Brexit UK nationals are third-country nationals for German immigration. Same consulate-dependent Blue Card window as other third-country corridors (28–84 days); fast-track when the employer opts in.

post_arrival_step.name: AIMA residence permit appointment
post_arrival_step.description: After entering on the long-stay visa, the applicant must obtain a residence permit via AIMA; appointment waits are tracked separately and are not included in low_days/high_days.

source.title: National (long-stay) visas — Portugal Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MNE)

entries.notes: Upper bound is the published statutory target for national visa decisions (60 days). The visa-stage range is kept honest by breaking the AIMA post-arrival residence-permit wait into post_arrival_step rather than rolling it into low/high days.
